method: Discrete-event twin, seed 2026. One 24 h household day through EgressGate (the only publisher of egress/<purpose>): 12 cloud-ASR voice requests (household opted in, provider must not store), nightly 48 MB encrypted backup, update checks every 6 h, AlarmHub supervision heartbeats every 300 s (plus, on the internet-down day only, a 14:00 leak alarm (AES-128 ADM-CID over a simulated WAN to a simulated centre)), 25 camera motion clips recorded locally while the camera firmware tries to upload each one, a fake plug that phones home every 10 min, one attempt to publish egress/ directly, and 200 local home-control commands confirmed by state. The same day is rerun with the internet down 00:00-24:00 (gate offline and WAN outage), then 1 h of internet back.

normal_day.what_left_the_house_today: Twelve voice requests for speech recognition, not stored, and last night's encrypted backup. No camera footage left the house. 169 attempts to send elsewhere were blocked (camera.front, plug.cheap).
normal_day.what_left_the_house_today_incl_routine: Twelve voice requests for speech recognition, not stored, last night's encrypted backup, 287 routine alarm-line check-ins, and four update checks. No camera footage left the house. 169 attempts to send elsewhere were blocked (camera.front, plug.cheap).

internet_down_day.what_left_the_house_today: Nothing left the house today. 169 attempts to send elsewhere were blocked (camera.front, plug.cheap).
internet_down_day.what_left_the_house_today_incl_routine: Nothing left the house today. 169 attempts to send elsewhere were blocked (camera.front, plug.cheap).

limitations: Byte sizes are modelled (Opus voice, 48 MB backup), not measured from real devices.

Home control uses a minimal stand-in device on the bus, not islab/twin; the 'unaffected' result shows no hidden dependency in our components, it does not test real device firmware that may itself require the cloud.

The gate only sees traffic that is routed through it. A device with its own route to the internet (own Wi-Fi uplink, cellular) bypasses it; in a real home this needs network enforcement (VLAN + firewall default-deny), which is not simulated.
Payload class is declared by the sender; the gate does not inspect content (an encrypted blob could contain anything). Encryption of backups is trusted from the sender's flag.
Internet-down day has no alternate alarm path (no cellular backup), so the centre only receives the leak alarm after the internet returns.
